Profile.name: Christopher Jennison
Profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer · Microsoft Copilot Studio
Profile.summary: Principal engineer and engineering leader with 13+ years of experience building AI platforms and the teams that run them. At Microsoft, I lead engineering for all of Copilot Studio's UI services, used by more than 230,000 organizations including 90% of the Fortune 500, and my team was one of the founding teams behind the new Copilot Studio experience built on the GitHub Copilot harness. I also built an internal AI agent platform that turns weeks of incident, accessibility, and compliance work into days. Before Microsoft, I ran a 25-engineer organization at Nuance and led engineering for the Nuance Mix UI, a conversational AI platform with $200M in annual recurring revenue.

strongestFit.label: Strongest fit
strongestFit.roles: Principal or Staff Engineer · Engineering Manager or Director · Head of AI Engineering

Profile.personalNote: I live in Manchester, New Hampshire, with my wife, our {age}-year-old daughter, and our dogs and cats.

map.title: Invented an AI agent platform for engineering operations
map.description: An internal platform that ingests engineering issues and works them end to end through a managed system of micro-agents. It grew into a dedicated engineering program that maintains, tests, and deploys its agents.

llmTesting.title: Built an LLM-powered live-site testing service
llmTesting.description: A hosted service in which LLM agents run real user scenarios against Copilot Studio's live websites, catching regressions before they become outages and cutting reliance on third-party testing vendors.

runCost.label: Cost of a full 100-scenario test run

nuanceMix.title: Led engineering for the Nuance Mix UI
nuanceMix.description: Built the team and the front end for Nuance Mix, the conversational AI toolset for designing IVR and chatbot experiences. Mix customers included HMRC, the IRS, New York Metro, and Rakuten.

eyecast.title: Shipped thermal anomaly detection for Florida power substations
eyecast.description: A thermal recognition system running on Raspberry Pi with dual-sensor cameras. It learns each site's own baseline and flags external temperature deviations on high-voltage equipment, pairing statistical models with GPU-powered reasoning to brief technicians.

microsoftPrincipal.title: Principal Engineering Manager
microsoftPrincipal.summary: Leads engineering across all Copilot Studio UI services. Founding team of the GitHub Copilot harness experience; built an internal AI agent platform for engineering operations.
highlights: Lead engineering for all of Copilot Studio's UI services, used by more than 230,000 organizations, owning delivery, quality, and live-site health for the experiences customers use to build, test, share, and run agents.

One of the founding teams of the new Copilot Studio customer experience built on the GitHub Copilot harness, now generally available; my team delivered its core platform for building agents and workflows.

Invented an internal AI agent platform that resolves engineering issues end to end, turning weeks of incident, accessibility, and compliance work into days; it now runs as a dedicated engineering program.
Built a hosted LLM-based live-site testing service that has saved millions of dollars in vendor costs at $40 per 100-scenario run.
Previously led Copilot Studio's end-of-funnel and viral features, including agent sharing and distribution for declarative and custom engine agents.

microsoftSenior.title: Senior Software Engineering Manager
microsoftSenior.summary: Led an international front-end team building Copilot Studio.
highlights: Led an international team of front-end engineers building Microsoft Copilot Studio, the low-code platform for building copilots and agents.
Scaled team processes for predictable delivery and clear reporting to leadership without putting deliverables at risk.
Joined Microsoft through its acquisition of Nuance Communications in March 2022.

eyecast.title: Machine Learning Engineer
eyecast.summary: Built thermal anomaly detection deployed to power substations across Florida.
highlights: Built thermal recognition models on Raspberry Pi with dual-sensor cameras that detect external temperature deviations on high-voltage equipment against self-established baselines.
Deployed across hundreds of cameras statewide in Florida, combining statistical methods with GPU-powered reasoning models to give technicians actionable reports.

highlights: Advised client companies on enterprise architecture and AI integration, from ideation through delivery.
